symptom: ako/mxcli#1542 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1614): "run --local: .mxcli/run-local.json disappears while the app is believed up (once after a trial-licence stop), and callers get no reason" — twice in one day the file was gone while the session treated the app as running; callers got HTTP 403 from the admin API and blamed credentials; `run status` gave no reason
cause: Three gaps on one path. (1) cmd_run.go deferred an UNCONDITIONAL removal of run-local.json in every `run --local` process, including `--setup`, which never publishes one and which the SessionStart hook runs on every session start, resume and compaction — so the hook deleted the live detached run's handshake, and oql/log fell back to default/.docker/.env credentials against a runtime that was up (403). (2) runtimeStoppedError read the stop reason from LocalRuntime.Log(), the JVM's stdout, but the licence's 'Maximum run time exceeded' is an application log line that only the file subscriber writes, to .mxcli/runtime.log — so the §60 reason detector never fired in a real run. (3) `run status` printed only the first line of the recorded error, and consumers turned a missing handshake into a credentials error
file: `cmd/mxcli/devloop_handshake.go` (`withdrawDevLoopHandshake` owner-pid check, `runStatusNote`); `cmd/mxcli/cmd_run.go` (state.Exit then withdraw); `cmd/mxcli/docker/runtime_stop_reason.go` (`RuntimeStoppedError`, `currentRuntimeLog`, `RuntimeLogStopReason`); `cmd/mxcli/docker/runstate.go` (`Reason`); `cmd/mxcli/cmd_run_lifecycle.go` (`statusLine` probes, missing-handshake warning); `cmd/mxcli/devloop_admin.go` (`devLoopAdminHint`); `cmd/mxcli/docker/m2ee.go` (`ErrAdminAuth`)
insight: A 403 is the discriminating detail: it needs a runtime that is UP, so 'the file is gone' could not have meant 'the run ended' — something else deleted it while the run lived, and the only other writer of that path was every other mxcli run process's deferred cleanup. Grep for every remover of a shared file and ask which processes reach it; the culprit here ran on a schedule nobody associated with the dev loop (SessionStart fires on resume and compaction too). Fix by ownership (remove only if the file's pid is yours), not by special-casing --setup, so a refused second run is covered as well. The second lesson: a reason detector tested on a string proves nothing about where the string lives — check which stream the runtime writes it to (application log -> file subscriber only) and read the newest boot's section of runtime.log (it is appended across restarts; an earlier boot's licence stop must not be blamed). Status must not turn 'handshake missing' into 'stopped' while the pid is alive and the app serves: `run status || run --detach` would then collide with the live run; report running and name the missing file. Controls: unconditional removal, first-line-only status and memory-only reason each make their test fail with the reported text
